The '''heavy industrial crane transport''', also known as '''HI-CT walker'''<ref name="2024 Encyclopedia" /> and referred to as the '''Trask walker''',<ref name="Art Book">[[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season Two)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season Two]]</ref> was a type of quadrupedal [[crane transport]] [[walker]] commonly used as [[cargo lifter]]s, employed on the [[Water|estuary]] [[moon]] [[Trask]],<ref name="Chapter 11" /> as well as the [[planet]]s [[Ferrix]]<ref name="Ferrix">{{Andor|Kassa (episode)}}</ref> and [[Cantonica]].<ref name="Outlaws">''[[Star Wars Outlaws]]''</ref>

==Description==
[[File:HI-CT-Outlaws.jpg|thumb|right|250px|An HI-CT being used around Canto Bight]]
Bearing some similarities to another crane transport, the [[Kuat Drive Yards]] manufactured [[OI-CT]],<ref name="2024 Encyclopedia" /> HI-CT walkers were well-balanced and heavily armored. Towering over Trask's seaside loading docks, they were more than powerful enough to lift a waterlogged [[ST-70 assault ship|ST-70 class Razor Crest M-111]] out of the sea.<ref name="Chapter 11" /> Each HI-CT possessed four sturdy legs and feet, as well as a crew deck and command bridge, alongside an extendable crane. The walker's legs were sealed thoroughly against sea water,<ref name="2024 Encyclopedia" /> though they were also sometimes utilized on land.<ref name="Ferrix" />

==History==
[[File:ZorbysWesternShiplot-Andor101.png|thumb|left|250px|HI-CTs seen in the distance on Ferrix]]
A number of heavy industrial crane transports could be found around [[Ferrix City]] on the [[planet]] [[Ferrix]]<ref name="Ferrix" /> in [[5 BBY]].<ref name="Andor Date">"That Would be me" takes place immediately after "[[Kassa (episode)|Kassa]]," which dates itself to [[5 BBY]].</ref> By [[3 ABY]],<ref name="OutlawsDate">{{OutlawsDate}}</ref> these walkers were employed around the [[South Stretch Worker's District|Worker's District]] of [[Canto Bight]] on the planet [[Cantonica]].<ref name="Outlaws" /> By [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Mando Date">{{MandoDate|S2|the crane's appearance}}</ref> HI-CT walkers could also be found patrolling the waters around a black market port on Trask. One such crane was used to retrieve the [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Din Djarin]]'s ship, the ''[[Razor Crest]]'', out of the sea after a failed landing during his [[mission to Trask]].<ref name="Chapter 11" /> That same year,<ref name="Mando Date" /> a similar yet distinct model of [[Mobile loading gantry|another model]] was used by the [[New Republic]] [[New Republic Correctional Corps|Correctional Corps]] across the [[Karthon Chop Fields]] on the moon [[Karthon]].<ref name="Believer">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 15: The Believer}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Trask-Walker-Concept.jpg|thumb|right|250px|HI-CT concept art by Christian Alzmann]]
This mobile loading gantry was first appeared in the [[2020]] ''[[The Mandalorian Season Two]]'' episode "[[Chapter 11: The Heiress]]," where it was described in the audio description.<ref name="Chapter 11" /> The shot with the gantry carrying the ''Razor Crest'' was realized in CG by [[Industrial Light & Magic]].<ref name="Effects">{{ILMVFXYouTube|video=Rd39daKZCI8|text=The Emmy-winning Special Visual Effects of The Mandalorian: Season Two}}</ref> [[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season Two)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season Two]] further labeled it specifically as a "Trask walker" in [[2022]], before the walker was finally officially identified as the "heavy industrial crane transport (HI-CT walker)" in an [[Wikipedia:Amazon (company)|Amazon]] pre-order listing preview for the book ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' which released on [[November 19]], [[2024]].<ref name="Edelweiss">{{LegacyEdelweiss|url=#sku=074409884X|text=Star Wars Encyclopedia|archiveurl=https://archive.vn/8tEJA}}</ref>

According to concept artist [[Christian Alzmann]], this walker was originally designed under the assumption that they were created from recycled [[All Terrain Armored Transport]] parts left over after the collapse of the [[Galactic Empire]],<ref name="Christian Alzmann">{{Twitter|CAlzmann|status/1561389499132719105|[[Christian Alzmann]]|quote=Rescuing the crashed Razorcrest on Trask. I figured with the empire defeated AT-AT parts would be plentiful. #starwars #themandalorian #conceptart #digitalart #razorcrest|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/JzBjw}}</ref> though this idea was later abandoned following the walker's appearances in projects such as ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]''<ref name="Ferrix" /> and ''[[Star Wars Outlaws]]''.<ref name="Outlaws" />
